title: test_a_seal_sweeps_first_and_says_so mints its dead minter with a subprocess, not os.fork, so the tester's sweep tooth runs on Windows
intention: test_a_seal_sweeps_first_and_says_so in test_the_teeth_that_measure_the_tester.py (os.fork at line 138) uses a subprocess child and runs on Windows.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 on akiendell: test_the_teeth_that_measure_the_tester.py reads 2 failed, 2 passed: test_a_seal_sweeps_first_and_says_so is AttributeError os.fork, test_hollow_reads_unran_exactly_the_file_the_sieve_names is the scratch bus (passfile 4b1c65ef9, not on main). os.fork does not exist on Windows, so the proofs that simulate a dead minter with a forked child cannot run there, and the Windows sweep (store.process_start read /proc and answered None for every pid) had NO tooth until 5b940b1c4fbe's own proof: the bug stood undetected as long as the only sweep proofs were POSIX-only.
traces_to: Law 8 (a proof that cannot run on a box proves nothing there), Law 3.
how: Replace the os.fork child with subprocess.Popen of a small python child that mints the scratch table and exits or is killed, keeping every assertion the proof makes; red-first is the AttributeError today, green once the child is a subprocess and 5b940b1c4fbe's Windows branch is in.
